faqs.q: What was the storm centre of the 1857 revolt where 21,000 taluqdars had their estates confiscated?
Which policy of the East India Company denied the right of succession to Hindu princes and caused suspicion among ruling princes?
faqs.e: The source lists 'Effective Control', 'Subsidiary Alliance' and 'Doctrine of Lapse' as policies causing political discontent; the denial of succession rights to Hindu princes is specifically tied to the Doctrine of Lapse.

faqs.q: On whose death in 1856 did Lord Canning announce that the next Mughal prince on succession would have to renounce the regal title and ancestral palaces?
The Religious Disabilities Act, which modified Hindu customs by declaring that a change of religion did not debar a son from inheriting his father's property, was passed in which year?

Consider the following statements regarding the outside events that coincided with the 1857 Revolt:
(I) The First Afghan War took place between 1838-42
(II) The Punjab Wars took place between 1845-49
(III) The Crimean War took place between 1854-56
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: The source cites all three conflicts as events in which the British suffered losses, creating a psychological impression that they could be defeated.

faqs.q: The General Service Enlistment Act, which required all future recruits to the Bengal Army to serve anywhere required by the government, was passed in which year?
faqs.e: This act, passed under Lord Canning's government, caused resentment as crossing the seas meant loss of caste for religious Hindus.

faqs.q: Sepoys serving in Sindh or Punjab were denied which allowance, causing dissatisfaction?
The annexation of which region, home to many sepoys, further inflamed their feelings before the revolt?

Consider the following statements regarding the economic causes of the 1857 Revolt:
(I) High tariff duties were imposed on Indian-made goods while British goods entering India attracted low tariffs
(II) By the mid-nineteenth century, exports of cotton and silk textiles from India had practically ended
(III) The destruction of Indian handicrafts was accompanied by the development of modern industries
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: The source states the destruction of handicrafts was NOT accompanied by development of modern industries, leaving skilled craftsmen without alternate employment.

faqs.q: Who made the observation, "It was the British intruder who broke up the Indian handloom and destroyed the spinning-wheel," in 1853?
What legal device did the British administration frequently use to forfeit the land rights of zamindars?
Which of the following was NOT among the administrative causes of discontent leading to the 1857 Revolt?

options.b: A foreign and alien character of British rule
options.d: Rampant corruption among police and petty officials

faqs.e: The Enfield rifle and its greased cartridges were the spark for the sepoy mutiny, not an administrative cause of the broader discontent.

faqs.q: British socio-religious reforms such as abolition of sati and support for widow remarriage were viewed by a large section of Indians as what?

options.b: Interference in social and religious domains

faqs.a: Interference in social and religious domains

faqs.q: What, besides mosque and temple lands being taxed, compounded socio-religious fears among Indians before 1857?
The greased cartridges of the Enfield rifle were rumoured to be made using the fat of which two animals?

.Consider the following statements regarding the discontent among sepoys before 1857:
(I) The sepoy was discriminated against racially and in matters of promotion and privileges
(II) The sepoy's discontent reflected the general disenchantment with British rule beyond military matters
(III) There had been no earlier history of revolts in the British Indian Army before 1857
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: The source records earlier revolts at Bengal (1764), Vellore (1806), Barrackpore (1825) and during the Afghan Wars (1838-42), so statement III is false.

faqs.q: According to S. Gopal's observation cited regarding the sepoy, the Army voiced grievances other than its own and the movement spread beyond what?
What did the reports about the mixing of bone dust in atta (flour), along with the Enfield rifle, do to the sepoys' disposition before the revolt?
The revolt began at Meerut on which date?
Meerut is located how far from Delhi?
Which unit refused to use the newly introduced Enfield rifle and mutinied at Berhampore in February 1857?
faqs.e: This regiment was disbanded in March 1857, before the main outbreak at Meerut.

faqs.q: Mangal Pande, who fired at the sergeant major of his unit at Barrackpore, belonged to which regiment?
On what date was Mangal Pande executed?

Consider the following statements regarding the events immediately preceding the outbreak at Meerut:
(I) On April 24, ninety men of the 3rd Native Cavalry refused to accept the greased cartridges
(II) On May 9, eighty-five of them were dismissed and sentenced to 10 years' imprisonment
(III) The general mutiny at Meerut broke out the same day the sentences were pronounced
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: The general mutiny broke out the next day, May 10, when the imprisoned comrades were released — not on the same day the sentences were pronounced.

faqs.q: Who was the political agent killed by the local infantry when Delhi was seized by the rebels?
Who offered resistance as the officer-in-charge of the magazine at Delhi before being overcome by the rebels?
Who was proclaimed the Emperor of India by the rebels after the seizure of Delhi?
Bahadur Shah Zafar's proclamation as Emperor is regarded as a recognition of what enduring fact?

options.a: That the British Crown had accepted Mughal rule
options.b: That Hindu princes had been restored their rights
options.c: That the Mughal dynasty had become the traditional symbol of India's political unity

faqs.a: That the Mughal dynasty had become the traditional symbol of India's political unity

faqs.q: To whom did Bahadur Shah write letters urging the organisation of a confederacy of Indian states against the British regime?

options.b: All the chiefs and rulers of India

faqs.a: All the chiefs and rulers of India

faqs.q: According to one estimate, of the roughly 1,50,000 men who died fighting the English in Awadh, over how many were civilians?

Consider the following statements regarding civilian participation in the 1857 Revolt:
(I) Peasants and petty zamindars attacked money-lenders and zamindars who had displaced them from land
(II) Rebels destroyed money-lenders' account books and debt records
(III) Civilian rebels avoided attacking British-established law courts and revenue offices
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: The source records that civilians did attack law courts, revenue offices (tehsils), revenue records and police stations, making statement III incorrect.

rows: General Bakht Khan (real command; nominal head Bahadur Shah Zafar)

faqs.q: Who led the Bareilly troops to Delhi and headed the court of soldiers that actually conducted the affairs of state in Bahadur Shah's name?
faqs.e: The court at Delhi consisted of ten members — six from the army and four from civilian departments.

faqs.q: Which of the following pairs of storm centre and leader is correctly matched?
Nana Saheb was the adopted son of which last Peshwa?
Who commanded the British station at Kanpur and surrendered to Nana Saheb on June 27, 1857?
faqs.e: Wheeler was killed on the same day he surrendered.

faqs.q: On what date did the rebellion break out at Lucknow?
Who was proclaimed Nawab of Awadh under Begum Hazrat Mahal's regency at Lucknow?
Who was killed during the siege of the residency at Lucknow?
Who finally evacuated the Europeans from Lucknow with the help of Gorkha regiments?

Kunwar Singh, who led the revolt in Bihar, was the zamindar of which place?
faqs.e: Kunwar Singh, then in his seventies, joined the sepoys when they reached Arrah from Dinapore (Danapur).

faqs.q: Maulvi Ahmadullah, an outstanding leader of the revolt at Faizabad, was originally a native of which region?
What was Rani Laxmibai's battle cry when driven out of Jhansi by British forces?
Whose adopted son was Lord Dalhousie refused permission to succeed to the throne of Jhansi, leading to the state's annexation under the Doctrine of Lapse?
faqs.e: Gangadhar Rao was Rani Laxmibai's husband.

faqs.q: Who paid tribute to Rani Laxmibai with the words, "Here lay the woman who was the only man among the rebels"?
Tantia Tope, who joined Rani Laxmibai after the loss of Kanpur, was a close associate of which leader?
Which local ruler decided to side with the English when Rani Laxmibai and Tantia Tope marched towards Gwalior?
Shah Mal, who organised the headmen and peasants of 84 villages against British rule, was based in which Pargana?
faqs.e: This area, in present-day Baghpat, Uttar Pradesh, was referred to as "chaurasi desh."

faqs.q: Shah Mal turned an irrigation department bungalow on the banks of which river into a "hall of justice"?
Who killed Shah Mal in July 1857?

Who led the siege of Delhi and later succumbed to injuries sustained during it?
Who publicly shot the royal Mughal princes at point blank range after their capture?

Sir Colin Campbell occupied Kanpur on which date?

Consider the following statements regarding the fate of the revolt's leaders:
(I) Nana Saheb escaped to Nepal in early 1859, never to be heard of again

Consider the following statements regarding participation in the 1857 Revolt:
(I) Big zamindars acted as "break-waters to storm" against the revolt
(II) Even Awadh taluqdars backed off once promises of land restitution were made
(III) Money-lenders and merchants actively supported the mutineers
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: Money-lenders and merchants suffered at the hands of the mutineers and saw their interests better protected under British patronage, so they did not support the revolt.

faqs.q: Educated Indians largely viewed the 1857 Revolt as what kind of movement?

options.a: Backward looking and supportive of the feudal order

faqs.a: Backward looking and supportive of the feudal order

faqs.q: Which ruler among the following did NOT participate in the revolt and instead gave active help to the British?
faqs.e: Rulers such as the Sindhia of Gwalior, the Holkar of Indore, the rulers of Patiala, Sindh, other Sikh chieftains, and the Maharaja of Kashmir refused to join.

faqs.q: By one estimate, not more than what fraction of the total population of India was affected by the revolt?
What kept the British commander-in-chief informed about the movements and strategy of the rebels?

options.c: Deep loyalty of the people to the Mughal Crown

faqs.a: Deep loyalty of the people to the Mughal Crown

faqs.q: Nana Saheb's aide Azimullah, an expert in political propaganda, belonged to which faith?
faqs.e: Rani Laxmibai, in turn, had the solid support of Afghan soldiers, illustrating cross-community cooperation on both sides.

options.a: It was entirely a war of independence

faqs.e: It was by this proclamation that the governor-general also acquired the additional title of 'Viceroy'.
